"I've been digging for months, following a trail of breadcrumbs that lead me to the darkest corners of the internet. I've seen things that no human should ever have to see. The blueprint, codenamed 'Erebus,' is a set of instructions for building a nuclear device capable of decimating an entire city. The implications are catastrophic. I know I'm taking a risk by sharing this information, but I have to warn someone. Please, you have to listen."

I pause, letting the silence of my safehouse stretch out for a fraction of a second. I keep my voice dropped to a harsh whisper, eyes locked on the encrypted progress bar on my monitor. 

"It started three days ago. A dead-drop file materialized on a secure server I haven't used since... since the blackout in Geneva. The one that cost me my team. It was just a string of hexadecimal code and a single phrase: *'The sun sets at midnight.'* It took me forty-eight straight hours to decrypt the routing protocols. It pulled me down into the Mariana Trench of the dark web—past the black markets, past the cartel hubs, into a ghost network that shouldn't mathematically exist. 

"Erebus isn't just a bomb. It's a localized irradiated fusion catalyst. I've stared at the schematics until my eyes bled. They've designed it to bypass every piece of non-proliferation tracking we have. It doesn't require weapons-grade uranium. Anyone with a high-end commercial fabricator and access to standard medical-grade isotopes could put it together. That’s the genius of it. That’s the horror. 

"I tried going to my old handlers at the Agency. But you know my history. They think I'm paranoid. They look at my discharge papers, they see the PTSD diagnosis, and they think the ghosts in my head have finally pushed me over the edge. They wouldn't even open the file. But I'm not crazy. I'm just the only one left who remembers what happens when we ignore the shadows. 

"Someone is auctioning this blueprint. The bidding closes in less than twelve hours, and the names I'm seeing on the ledger... they aren't governments. They're zealots. If this falls into their hands, millions of people will burn before they even realize the sky has caught fire. 

"I'm sending you a packet of encrypted data. It contains the mirrored IP node of the auction site and the fragments of the blueprint I managed to scrape before the firewall locked me out. I need you to trace the host. I can't do this alone anymore. 

"My proximity alarms are flashing. They know someone breached their servers, and it's only a matter of time before they triangulate my signal. If they find me before we shut this down... well, I don't plan on being taken alive this time. 

"Just... look at the files. Stop this. Before Erebus wakes up."
